title: Who Remembers What? Multi-Granularity Memory Extraction for Multi-User, Multi-Agent Interaction
why: MixUA distills user-agent trajectories into lessons and scopes them to a user-agent pair, user, agent, or global store so group-evolving agents can share skills, memory, and harness-code lessons without leaking private facts. CrossLearnBench probes both transfer and privacy. Core retained lesson-sharing for self-evolving / group-evolving agents.
mechanism: Independent trajectories are distilled into lessons and assigned a scope by who benefits and what may be disclosed. Lessons stay in the matching store so later runs by other users or agents can reuse them when permitted.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): with five users and seven agents, MixUA raises pass rates by up to 16 points over no memory and 5 over a single global memory, including on tasks previously tried only by other users on other agents. It retains up to 90% of previously stated preferences, and at most 0.02% of privacy probes find a planted private fact in a forbidden scope.

title: LongCapHarness: Capability-Guided Auto-Harnessing for Long-Context Reasoning
why: LongCapHarness recursively revises capability-primitive implementations, capability state, and control logic on a development set via recursive self-improvement, with no data synthesis or LLM post-training. Direct harness-level RSI for long-context reasoning.
mechanism: The harnessing process recursively revises and updates capability primitive implementation, capability state, and control logic through recursive self-improvement on the development set. The resulting harness is applied to Llama3-8B and transferred to Qwen2.5-3B without weight training.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): LongCapHarness substantially outperforms recent data-synthesis-based baselines on HELMET and RULER; estimated development cost is less than 50% of the estimated training costs of NExtLong and PolicyLong.

title: Agent Self-Improvement with Frozen Weights: The Added Value and Limits of Failure Traces
why: Tests whether notes around a frozen-weight agent (the harness) improve when a teacher writes them from the agent's failure traces, versus a matched search that never sees those traces. Retained-notes / harness-learning study with an accept-if-better-scoring process and reported limits, including a null on full conversations.
mechanism: Actor weights stay fixed (open 9B model). A larger teacher writes harness notes. One process tries notes and keeps better-scoring ones; a comparison arm writes notes from failure traces. A separate screen admits single lessons for later tests.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on generated customer-service decisions, notes based on the agent's mistakes improved accuracy by 4.0 percentage points over notes from the same process with mistakes withheld; the try-and-keep process alone reached about 60% of the total improvement. In full customer-service conversations the same notes showed no demonstrated improvement. A strict screen admitted two customer-service lessons still awaiting tests on new data, and one tool-use lesson written without seeing mistakes, which showed no demonstrated gain on new tool-use tasks. A blind audit judged 146 of 240 tool-use test items defective.

title: JoMoHa: Joint Model--Harness Optimization with Reinforcement Learning
why: JoMoHa jointly trains an executable harness-generation policy and a task-execution policy with RL, after documenting that alternating weight-only or harness-only updates can become incompatible. The harness component is central to the claimed RSI loop, even though weights are also updated.
mechanism: A harness-generation policy and a task-execution policy are trained jointly through reinforcement learning on the agent's own generated trajectories, rather than alternating isolated weight or harness updates.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): JoMoHa outperforms the evaluated weight-only and harness-only baselines and achieves the highest success rates among the evaluated methods on ALFWorld, WebShop, and DBBench, averaging 70.3% and reaching 97.0% on ALFWorld. The authors describe this as recursive self-improvement.

title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
why: InfraRSI is an agentic harness that co-optimizes training-launch knobs and code patches under a fixed task contract, re-verifies candidates against a baseline, and writes accepted findings to a cross-hardware experience bank. RSI of non-weight training infrastructure, also on HF Papers 2026-11-10.
mechanism: A five-stage workflow (init, doctor, run, report, apply) locks editable scope and invariants, co-optimizes launch settings and code patches, re-verifies top candidates, and commits promoted changes. Experience-seeded configurations and global execution-time / censored peak-memory models guide later trials; priors are revised from live runs and findings are logged to an experience bank.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across four single- and multi-node dense and MoE LLM workloads, InfraRSI achieves a speedup of up to 2.75× and lifts mean Model FLOPs Utilization from 17.4% to 30.0%, outperforming evaluated tuners and coding agents while transferring experience across GPUs.

title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
why: EmoHarness runs a frozen multimodal student inside a harness (prompts, settings, and verification code). In Meta-Harness Evolving, a stronger Builder LLM reads errors and traces offline, edits the harness, and keeps edits only if they pass static checks and validation gates; the Builder never sees evaluation items. Direct meta-harness evolution with an accept/retain rule.
mechanism: A human-written scaffold numbers visual, transcript, and prosody evidence and has the frozen student weigh candidate emotions against it. Offline, a Builder LLM edits the harness from the student's errors and execution traces; static checks and validation gates decide which edits are kept.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on 5,507 MME-Emotion items, EmoHarness raises task-macro Recognition by 7.6-13.4 points over a single video-only call for all four students and both Builders. Transcripts and prosody descriptions supply most of this boost (+5.38 to +10.71); the scaffold changes the audio-augmented call by -0.79 to +2.54, and evolved edits add at most +0.95, although no evolved increment survives Holm correction. Transfer to IntentQA is small and does not survive correction.

title: SkillDuet: Co-Evolving Models and Skills through Response Feedback
why: SkillDuet co-evolves LLM parameters and a persistent textual skill set (Global): skills extracted from on-policy trajectories guide weight updates, while a response-based Strength score selects skills to consolidate. The skill-library half is a retained, co-evolving non-weight component and is described as skill-level RSI.
mechanism: Skills extracted from on-policy trajectories guide parameter updates through OPD at every step. A Strength score ranks candidate skills by the shift they induce in the current model's responses; the highest-scoring skills are periodically consolidated into a persistent global skill set that, with the updated model, guides later interactions.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): with Qwen3-4B, SkillDuet achieves success rates of 98.57% on ALFWorld and 92.97% on WebShop, exceeding the matched SEED-API baseline by 2.86 and 5.47 percentage points. Ablations are reported for response-based skill selection and Global consolidation. Further experiments say benefits of retained skills depend on content and compatibility with the model.

title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery
why: SciMARS recursively adapts a multi-agent scientific-discovery harness: separate component editors revise roles, coordination, and (in the +Memory variant) how agents record, retrieve, and receive evidence, with candidate probes selecting the next harness. Shared evidence graph plus retained harness edits.
mechanism: A shared evidence graph stores observations. Separate editors adapt roles and coordination; SciMARS + Memory adds a third editor for record/retrieve/receive policies. Candidate probes guide composition and selection of the next harness for the task.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): evaluated through experimental-data replay and a digital twin. SciMARS + Memory resolves 12/18 GPT-6-Astra and 2/18 GLM-5.3 attempts on Autonomous Science Bench, versus 8/18 and 1/18 for the base multi-agent team. On ScienceAgentBench and AppWorld, it solves 14/38 and 11/20 tasks, versus 11/38 and 5/20 for the base team.

title: REINS: A Self-Evolving Agent Harness for Real-Time Trajectory Planning
why: REINS is a self-evolving agent harness for real-time trajectory planning: LLM proposals are grounded, verified, and consolidated into an indexed rule memory that later scenes can use without re-invoking the LLM. Frozen weights; memory matures from verified novel scenes.
mechanism: LLM outputs are grounded to a learned variable-level dynamics model, verified via calibrated predicates and forward rollout, and consolidated into an indexed rule memory served in O(log n). Familiar scenes resolve by memory lookup; novel scenes invoke the LLM, whose verified outputs enrich the memory. LLM weights are not modified.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): without modifying LLM weights, REINS attains 98%+ compliance, nearly 50% collision reduction, and 1.9-4.6 ms latency on simulated and real-world benchmarks at the tactical decision layer, with LLM invocation rate monotonically declining as memory matures. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Track) per abs comment.

title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement with Statistical Guarantees
why: TRUST is a gating framework for recursive harness updates: it adapts an online multiple-hypothesis testing procedure so agents decide which harness changes to keep, aiming to control false evolution while still accepting beneficial updates. Evaluation science for harness-level RSI accept/retain rules.
mechanism: An online multiple-hypothesis testing procedure is adapted to control the rate of false evolution across rounds. An LLM analyzing historical context helps set how much evidence is required to replace the incumbent harness. The framework is aimed at agents that refine their own harnesses without retraining the underlying LLM.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): the authors prove, under stated assumptions, a limit on the proportion of accepted updates that result in unacceptable performance loss, and derive a lower bound on final performance gain. Across HotpotQA, DROP, and APPS with DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen-3.8-Flash, TRUST reduces the average ratio of accepted inferior updates from the greedy gate's 45.59% to 2.78%, while achieving higher final scores than the evaluated state-of-the-art statistical gate baselines.

title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
why: SimplEvo lets an MLLM improve under direct control by retaining self-written text memories: a coordinate-free task memory from one demonstration, plus a bounded working memory refined after each training episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery, then frozen at test time. No weight updates. Embodied memory-evolution baseline against heavier RSI harnesses.
mechanism: The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a train-test protocol it creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. No weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, it reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With memories fixed, it also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scenes. A working memory written by GPT-6-Astra can be reused as-is by weaker MLLMs.

title: When Experience Becomes a Backdoor: Poisoning Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Failure-Aware Task Optimization
why: Audit/attack paper on self-evolving agents that distill execution experience into persistent reusable skills. BadEvolve poisons only evolution tasks so a trusted evolver implants backdoors into its own skills, with failure-aware updates across induction, activation, following, and effect. In-scope negative result / security audit of skill self-evolution.
mechanism: The attacker injects poisoned evolution tasks rather than editing the victim's skill store. BadEvolve diagnoses attack failures across Induction, Activation, Following, and Effect, directs updates toward the failing stage, rolls back to preserve earlier progress, and uses failure memory to avoid repeating ineffective updates.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): extensive experiments across diverse self-evolution frameworks, benchmarks, and backbone LLMs are said to demonstrate the effectiveness of BadEvolve. Quantitative tables are not in the abstract.

title: What Does a Harness Repair? Four Preregistered Studies Around a Longevity-Tuned Language Model
why: v4 retitles the work and adds a fourth preregistered study on class ratio of the GEPA search set (CREAK and resolved Manifold; descriptive after recorded deviation D001), plus a licences section—method/experiment expansion versus corpus v1 (single preregistered study of visibility, baseline adequacy, and evaluation defects in harness search).
mechanism: Harness search around a frozen model still keeps a change if it raises a score. v4 reports four preregistered studies, including a new fourth study that varies search-set skew and objective on CREAK and resolved Manifold questions; those fourth-study results are descriptive because render hashes were not committed before the first replication call (D001).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v4 abs): first two studies and a 14B GEPA comparison are restated (including that two GEPA harnesses beat thinking off by 34 test points but were not detectably above the strongest constant label). In the third study, GEPA beat the constant on FPB (confirmatory); thinking off was not meaningfully worse than any BoolQ harness; 3 of 4 MMLU-Pro searches kept their seed. On exploratory Autocast, harnesses were within 0.7 points of the constant. In the fourth study, minority-recall estimates were lower at 80:20 than at 50:50 in all four test cells; the balanced objective and re-selection from each search's pool had higher minority- and lower majority-recall estimates in all four cells; five of eight minority-recall intervals included zero. The authors say this does not show that skew explains the earlier collapse.
